name.description: The organisation's own name, as it prints it. Scheme files that belong to this organisation must carry exactly this string in their `organisation` field.

kind.description: national-body stands alone; affiliate is a body under a national one; club is where people train. These are structural words, chosen to be generic across countries, and are never reader-facing: the BJA calls its affiliates the home nations, a German federation would say Landesverband, and the site renders whatever the organisation itself says - the kind only decides how the chain may link.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, as scheme files use (GB, JP).

parent.description: The organisation this one belongs to: an affiliate names its national body (required), a club names its national body or affiliate (optional). A national body has no parent. The chain is how everything derives - a reader's country comes from the top of it, and opting in stacks the voices along it.

schemes.description: The grading schemes this organisation owns, by scheme id. Opting into the organisation's view can then offer its schemes, and vice versa. Ownership means it published the transcribed document: JudoScotland's Kyu syllabus is claimed by JudoScotland even though the Kyu pathway is the BJA family's, which the parent link records.

exams.description: The examinations this organisation sets, by exam id, so the offer-list for a body is a lookup rather than a string match. Checked both ways against each exam's own `organisation` field.

localisedText.description: Text by BCP 47 language code; "en" required, other languages optional.

title: organisation
description: A governing body, an affiliate body, or a club whose voice appears in perspectives/. Not a provider (those publish demonstration videos) and not a channel (those are places to browse): an organisation OWNS content - its grading schemes, its examinations, and its per-technique perspectives. The organisation id is the filename.
